publick: archaic spelling of 'public'; meaning the general public or community
annum: Latin for 'per year'; used here to mean each year
expence: old spelling of 'expense'; the cost or money spent on something
carcass: the dead body of a child, considered as meat for food
plump: fat and well-fed, describing a healthy infant meant for eating
breeders: women of childbearing age who are having children
beggars: poor people who depend on charity to survive
raiment: clothing or garments worn on the body
sustenance: food and drink needed to keep someone alive
nourishment: food that provides the substance needed for growth and health
livelihood: the means of earning enough money to live on
desire: here, to ask for or request something formally
maturely: after careful, deliberate thought and long consideration
computed: calculated or worked out by careful arithmetic
reckoned: calculated, counted, or estimated as a total amount
subtract: take away a number or amount from a total
liable: likely to suffer something or be subject to a condition
wanting: lacking or missing something that is needed
cottagers: people who live in small, humble cottages, usually poor laborers
labourers: workers who do hard manual work for wages
tenants: people who rent land or a house from a landlord
landlords: owners who rent out land or houses to others for payment
sterling: British money of standard value, the pound sterling
commodity: a product or good that can be bought, sold, or traded
exportation: the act of sending goods out of a country to sell abroad
manufacture: the making of goods, especially on a large scale
expedients: practical means chosen to solve a problem or reach a goal
entertainment: a feast or hospitable meal offered to guests
dishes: prepared foods or courses served at a meal
dressing: the preparing and cooking of meat for a meal
tables: dinner tables where food is served to guests and family
quality: people of high social rank or the upper class
refinement: good taste, polished manners, and cultivated delicacy
prime: of the best or highest quality, in excellent condition
honest: decent, respectable, and morally upright in character
gentlemen: men of good family and high social standing
acquaintance: people one knows slightly, though not as close friends
stock: livestock, the animals kept on a farm for breeding or use
cattle: domestic farm animals such as cows, kept for meat or labor
breed: to raise or bring forth young, especially livestock or children
confess: to admit openly that something is true
objection: an argument or reason raised against a proposal
offering: a proposal put forward for consideration or acceptance
males: male children, the boys in a family
females: female children, the girls in a family
babes: very young infants or small children
subject: liable or exposed to something, such as a tax or condition
alive: still living, not yet dead, in good health
